activity_context.topic_title: The Cartesian Equation of a Plane

feedback.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5 \\ 2x+z & =5 \\ 2x+z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
